masteryZone.q: Suppose a local municipal authority in Bengal Presidencies imposes a house tax on all merchants in 1815. Under 3. Crown Sovereignty & Local Governance, assess the legality of this tax and what measures could be taken in case of non-payment.
masteryZone.sol: The tax is fully legal. The Charter Act of 1813 empowered local governments to impose taxes on persons subject to their jurisdiction and authorized them to punish non-payment with fines, penalties, or property confiscation.

masteryZone.q: Explain EIC's 'trustee' status under the Crown sovereignty assertion of 3. Crown Sovereignty & Local Governance.
masteryZone.sol: By explicitly declaring the Crown's sovereignty, the Act established that the territories and revenues held by EIC belonged to the British state. EIC did not own India; it was merely permitted to govern as a trustee on behalf of the Crown for 20-year intervals.
